reasons: Default secret key and database password are placeholders that must be changed before real use.
The database address here uses localhost, which will not work inside Docker without changing it.
Some listed settings, such as UPLOAD_DIR, are not read by the settings file shown.

terms.meaning: A plain text file of name and value pairs that the app reads at startup to set options.
A secret code that proves to an outside service, such as OpenAI, that the app is allowed to use it.
A switch that turns a feature on or off without changing code.
A browser rule that decides which websites may call the app. Here it is set by the allowed origins list.
A fast helper store used for background job coordination.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Full settings template
sections.what: Lists every setting the app can use, grouped by purpose: database, cache, environment, AI provider keys, Qualtrics, security, allowed websites, feature switches, model choices, file storage and compliance.
sections.why: Serves as a single reference for setup, so the owner does not have to read the settings code.
sections.watch_out: Never type a real key or password into this template, because it is usually shared or committed.

summary: A template listing every setting the app reads from its environment file, with placeholder values to copy and fill in.
purpose: Gives the owner a ready-made list of settings so the app can be set up without guessing names.
why: Likely reason: keeps real secrets out of the code while still showing which settings exist.
how: Copy this file to a file named .env, fill in real values such as API keys and the database password, and then start the app. The app reads the names in this file when it starts.
inputs: The owner's own keys, passwords and feature choices.
outputs: None on its own. It is a template the app reads through its settings file.
risks: If real keys are typed into this template and it is committed to version control, the keys are exposed. The default SECRET_KEY and dev password are weak placeholders.
debug: If the app says a setting is missing or wrong, compare the names here with the names in the config file. Check that the copied file is named .env exactly.
